Large optimization models are often made of independent blocks that interact only
through a few **linking variables** or a few **linking constraints**. Decomposition
methods exploit exactly this. Benders decomposition [@benders1962] fixes the linking
variables and lets the blocks answer with cuts. Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition
[@dantzig1960] prices the linking constraints and lets the blocks answer with columns.
